Drug choice conditional on kidney function/heart failure — management only.
'Refer urgently' (emergency) vs 'refer same day' (urgency) is a referral-urgency difference, not an explicit page escalation to Emergency; single Urgent level is consistent with the briefing.

elements.scope_reason: Confirmation of ≥180/110 after 1 hour rest and ≥3 readings is a multi-reading condition; the language can only test the current BP measurement.
parts_missing: BP confirmed ≥ 180/110 as evidence for severe hypertension

elements.scope_reason: 'Diagnose mild hypertension' is a flowchart diagnosis, but it requires BP 140/90–159/99 on 2 further occasions ≥ 2 days apart — not representable within one encounter; SNOMED has no 'mild hypertension' (closest 'Stage 1 hypertension' finding).
As for mild: 'Diagnose moderate hypertension' (BP 160/100–179/109 on repeat readings); repeat-visit criterion not representable; closest concept 'Stage 2 hypertension'.
Fragment ('hypertension') of the 'Diagnose moderate hypertension' node; judged with p148-1a771248.
'Diagnose severe hypertension' after BP confirmed ≥ 180/110 is a diagnostic conclusion; a single-encounter possible rule on BP ≥ 180/110 would be expressible, though confirmation-after-rest is not.
parts_missing: asymptomatic BP ≥ 180/110 has no rule at all

rule_level_problems.problem: The lower flowchart's diagnostic conclusions (Diagnose mild / moderate / severe hypertension) have no rules. Mild/moderate need repeat readings on later visits (arguably not representable), but severe hypertension on BP ≥ 180/110 without symptoms could at least be a possible rule; as written, an asymptomatic patient with BP 200/120 gets no diagnosis and no priority.

Lists the 16 raw findings instead of referencing (active_condition …) for stroke / hypertensive emergency / urgency / heart failure as the briefing pattern describes; functionally equivalent here. 'Severe headache' appears twice (with and without Sudden onset) — redundant but harmless.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable stroke with BP ≥ 180/110 (hypertension diagnosis)
rule_level_problems.problem: Weakness evidence uses generic 'Muscle weakness' (sudden onset) rather than limb weakness/hemiparesis, so any sudden generalised weakness with high BP yields probable stroke.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable hypertensive emergency / Diagnose probable hypertensive urgency
rule_level_problems.problem: Severe headache with SBP ≥ 180 fires both emergency and urgency probable diagnoses at once; this mirrors the page (severe headache is listed under both) but the rules do not express the page's implied precedence of emergency over urgency.

summary: The red box is fully and correctly encoded: thresholds (180/110, 180/130), and/or logic, every criterion, the four 'likely' diagnoses (stroke, hypertensive emergency, hypertensive urgency, heart failure), and an Urgent priority, with eGFR cut-offs reasonably mapped to CKD stage 5 / renal impairment. The main gap is the lower flowchart: no rule diagnoses mild, moderate or severe hypertension, so asymptomatic BP ≥ 180/110 produces nothing. That gap is borderline because repeat-visit confirmation can't be represented. Minor: generic 'Muscle weakness' for one- or two-sided weakness, and the priority rule doesn't reference the likely diagnoses through active_condition.
